items.title: Explore Chicago first and Denver second

items.title: Define the desired qualities of the new home
items.description: Charm is flexible; safety, dog access, parking, privacy, gym access, natural light, location, space, and size guide comparison.

items.title: Secure a Home

items.description: Discuss refill timing, what history or documentation can be provided, and how to bridge care until a new provider is established.

items.title: Save provider and pharmacy contact information
items.description: Keep Dr. Dippo's office and the current pharmacy details somewhere easy to reach after the move.

items.title: Define the functional first-72-hours kit
items.description: Food, cleaning supplies, self-care, eating basics, and Marvel’s bowls, crate, food, and place.

items.title: Plan for holiday and family returns
items.description: Mom’s October 1 birthday, the expected November birth, Thanksgiving, Christmas, and my December 27 birthday need one travel-and-money view.

items.title: Set up utilities, mail forwarding, a new pharmacy, and address updates
items.description: Utilities, internet, insurance, parking, building reservations, mail, payroll, bank, pharmacy, and registration wait for a real address.

items.description: Confirm volume, route, address, hitch fit, and rental cost before committing. Chicago is the leading route.

items.title: Get the final transportation quote
items.description: Quote the chosen option for the real route and date.

items.title: Confirm loading and parking access at the new building
items.description: Loading dock, elevator reservation, and where a trailer or truck can park.

items.title: Research the car + hitch + small trailer option
items.description: Researched as the likely lower-cost route.

items.title: Consider a U-Haul truck as the alternative
items.description: Considered; likely more expensive.

items.title: Write the Move Day care plan
items.description: Protect documents, valuables, medication, Marvel’s travel, food, sleep, and communication.

items.title: Keep departure and arrival proof
items.description: Save confirmations, receipts, address changes, utility shutoff records, and unit-condition photos while completing the related actions.

items.title: Use the desired life as the decision filter
items.description: Choose what supports a safe, alive, creative home without making work the whole identity.

items.title: Romanticize life into a new thriving routine
items.description: Plants, movement, a rustic breakfast, exploration, useful work, friends, music, reading, games, movies, and rest.

items.title: Keep music and creative growth central
items.description: Creativity is a true motivation, not an upgrade to add after everything else is solved.

items.title: Carry love forward without carrying every problem
items.description: Ask family for excitement about the move and growing independence—not a constant transfer of crises.

items.title: Choose simple rhythms for Baltimore relationships
items.description: Keep close friends, Mom, Sister, and Grandma visible without requiring the old relationship shape to stay unchanged.

items.title: Create a weekly intention and transition ritual
items.description: Use music, sunlight, reflection, wonder, and weekly check-ins to hold fear without turning it into a requirement.

items.title: Keep a few low-pressure Chicago and Denver doors visible
items.description: Meg, electronic music and vocal spaces, drum and bass, a gym/PT rhythm, nature, and one recurring social place to discover.

plans.title: Cash Flow for the Move
plans.question: Can I cover my current obligations, move-in costs, the physical move, and still have usable cash after arriving?
plans.outcome: Arrive with bills covered, move-in and transport paid for, and usable cash left over—without counting pending money as money I already have.
plans.summary: Unknown costs still need real numbers.

plans.title: Get Approved & Secure a Home
plans.question: What income, credit, documentation, and housing route will get me approved for a workable home?
plans.outcome: A signed lease or workable sublet at a home I actually want, backed by income and credit evidence a landlord accepts—ending in a confirmed address.

plans.title: Physical Move Plan
plans.question: What is the most practical and affordable way to move me, Marvel, my car, and my belongings once the destination and timing are real?
plans.outcome: Have a practical, affordable transportation plan that gets me, Marvel, the car, and my belongings to the new home safely.

plans.title: Medication & Essential Continuity
plans.question: What do I need to prepare before leaving so medication and essential care continue through the transition?
plans.outcome: Maintain medication continuity through the move and establish a workable next-provider/pharmacy route without having to reconstruct treatment history from scratch.

instructions.title: Pending money is not cash
instructions.body: Unemployment and pending resale count toward the projection, never toward cash available now.

instructions.title: Move-in cost depends on the property
instructions.body: Application fees ($50–$100), deposit, pet and parking costs vary—use the real listing, including verified specials.

instructions.title: When money arrives
instructions.body: Mark the expected entry received and update the account balance so it is not counted twice.

instructions.title: Typical approval rules
instructions.body: Income around 2.5–3× rent and a 625+ credit score are common targets, but every property sets its own final rule.

instructions.title: Unemployment is bridge cash
instructions.body: It helps pay bills while searching but should not be assumed to count as rental income proof.

instructions.title: Build the application packet
instructions.body: ID, a signed offer letter with compensation or new-role paystubs, and a factual credit explanation only if a property asks.

instructions.title: Hitch required for the trailer route
instructions.body: The car needs an installed hitch before a trailer is an option.

instructions.title: Exact cost depends on destination and date
instructions.body: Trailer and truck pricing changes with the route and the move date.

instructions.title: Belongings volume changes the right option
instructions.body: Selling and releasing more makes the smaller trailer more realistic.

instructions.title: A larger truck is likely more expensive
instructions.body: And the car still has to get there.

instructions.title: Building rules may matter
instructions.body: Loading docks, elevator reservations, and parking or trailer access can all constrain move day.

instructions.title: What to prepare
instructions.body: Request pharmacy fill history and useful provider information before moving.

instructions.title: What to ask the current provider
instructions.body: Discuss the move, refill timing, treatment history, and what documentation may be useful during the transition.

instructions.title: What a new provider may ask for
instructions.body: Pharmacy history, prior prescriber contact, treatment history, ID, and insurance information.

instructions.title: Understand what happens before transferring care
instructions.body: Some prescriptions cannot simply transfer across state lines—learn the steps before relying on a new pharmacy.
